A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-pattern benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3–6 report original experiments evaluating LLMs on synthetic graph-pattern tasks and real-world molecular, social, biological and fingerprint datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds empirical strategy frequencies, error analyses and chain-of-thought prompting results in Appendices G–I.

M1.justification: The benchmark and its extraction, filtering and classification procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 2–3 document procedures already described in v1 Sections 5.2–5.3. CoT is evaluated as a supplementary prompting variant rather than incorporated into the core pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same nine primitive patterns, synthetic graph datasets and ten real-world datasets. The additional analyses and CoT experiments use existing tasks and graph scales without introducing new dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The original seven-model roster and real-world comparison membership are retained. Appendix I, Table 25 adds an explicit comparison between zero-shot and CoT prompting for Gemini and O1-mini.

E3.justification: Supplementary evaluations introduce three reasoning demonstrations for CoT, manual inspection of 10% of outputs, separate precision/recall analysis, and aggregation across encodings, scales and patterns for rankings. The original model versions, graph scales and dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1’s isomorphism-strategy and node-degree analyses, Appendices G–I add a broad strategy taxonomy and occurrence frequencies, generation-error examples, selected-node degree analysis, detection precision/recall diagnostics, a k-core failure example and CoT sensitivity experiments.

E5.justification: Both report 50 pattern-translation trials and 100 frequent-subgraph iterations. Neither provides confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-variability analysis. The new descriptive frequencies and rankings do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises several accuracy/diversity entries, including O1-mini’s average diversity from 0.84 to 0.78. Tables 20 and 22–25 add rankings, strategy frequencies, degree statistics, precision/recall and CoT results. Tables 3–10 and the original full detection tables retain their numbers. Some Table 25 zero-shot values conflict with Tables 18–19, limiting direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The Transformer–LOCAL simulation theorem, formal statement, Lemmas 1–3 and supporting proof are retained, moving from Appendix B to Appendix A. The added evaluation pseudocode does not introduce new theoretical results or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract’s third finding changes from LLM strategies differing from conventional algorithms to diverse algorithm choices whose performance depends on execution capability. The central benchmark contribution, eleven-task/seven-model scope and other headline claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 7.2 replaces the broad adjacency-list/attention-locality explanation with task-dependent alignment between graph encodings and algorithms. Appendices H–I substantially expand interpretations of unintended edges, overlooked-edge errors, degree-threshold failures and circumstances where CoT provides limited benefit.

D1.justification: v2 adds a dataset/implementation access link, SMILES-to-graph conversion instructions, molecular description examples and combined prompts, and extraction/evaluation pseudocode. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that the original procedures changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zheng et al. (2023) when discussing LLM identification of molecular SMILES patterns. It removes Hu et al. (2019) on attributed motif discovery and Xiao et al. (2023) on attention sinks. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence are retained. Editing concentrates on the abstract, frequent-subgraph explanation and empirical-insights discussion, alongside appendix relabeling, new supplementary sections, publication headers and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and reorganizes the displays through molecular-description tables, pseudocode boxes and analytical tables. Figures 7–8 visualize existing detection results across all scales, while Appendix J redisplays retained results in separate adjacency-list and edge-list tables. Several original displays are repositioned.

improvement.justification: The added preprocessing and prompt documentation, pseudocode and broader failure analyses improve transparency and interpretability. These gains are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: Table 2 changes mean square accuracy from 0.58 to 0.27 despite unchanged component values, and Table 25 contains zero-shot values inconsistent with the detection tables. The documentation and diagnostic gains support a limited overall improvement, while the claimed CoT gains require clarification.
